liam: Heads up — after merging auto-kernel selector v2 we saw a small but reproducible perf/regression on the paged-attn path. P99 up ~2.3% and a few OOMs during the 80-token smoke tests.

carmen: ugh. which workloads? hosted or dedicated?

liam: Mainly hosted inference tail on medium-concurrency (50-100 rps per GPU) with mixed seqs (8/64/256). Dedicated perf tests also show increased workspace churn in the profiler.

sasha: any kernel mismatch logs? can perf-bot dump the selection matrix?

perf-bot: kernel-selection matrix for run 2249991111-rt: 
```
model: redwood-v1-medium
seq_profile: {p8:0.35, p64:0.45, p256:0.20}
auto-kernel: selected tiled-attn-vec (default), fallback: block-attn
observed: increased temp_ws_allocs, higher realloc rate
```

ajay: I repro'd locally with the synthetic replay. The allocator is doing more small allocations -> fragmentation. The new kernel's workspace pattern interleaves buffers differently so free lists are less reuse-friendly.

liam: profiler snapshot (abridged):
```
GPU0: total_mem=40.0GB used=31.2GB free=8.8GB
heap_allocs: 12.3k allocs/s -> 18.6k allocs/s (after v2)
avg_realloc_size: 48KB -> 52KB
fragmentation_est: 9% -> 18%
OOM_events: 0 -> 3 (10m window)
```

carmen: sounds like two levers: allocator headroom/workspace sizing, and kernel packing (how kernels order their temp buffers). We can mitigate quickly by tuning allocator & KV compaction thresholds.

sasha: propose quick experiments:
- bump allocator headroom from 128MB -> 256MB for tiled-attn path
- cap per-request workspace to 48MB for short seqs, keep large seqs unchanged
- lower KV compaction threshold (trigger earlier) from 0.6 -> 0.45 to reduce live footprint
- revert to previous kernel for p64-heavy slices as an A/B (canary)

ajay: did a quick smoke: bumping headroom to 256MB lowered realloc rate by ~22% and fragmentation estimate back to ~11%. Tail latency improved ~1.4% but still not baseline. KV compaction tweak shaved another ~0.7% tail.

liam: good. still have a delta ~0.2-0.3% P99. Could be kernel working set ordering. Can we try a microkernel variant that concatenates temporaries to improve locality?

carmen: implementable as kernel flag: `--temp-layout=concatenate` vs `interleave`. We can A/B at routing layer quickly.

perf-bot: scheduled experiment `exp/kal-2249991111`:
- 50k reqs replay (mixed seq)
- variants: baseline(v1), auto-kernel-v2, v2+headroom256, v2+headroom256+concatenate-temp
- results ETA: 2h

ajay: also logging note: set `KV.compact_on_threshold=true` for that experiment so we can measure compaction cost. Add `kv_compact_profile=true` to traces.

liam: action items:
- ajay: run v2+headroom256+concatenate-temp with kv profiling, collect nvprof and kv-evict charts (owner: @ajay)
- sasha: add canary route to force previous kernel for p64-heavy traffic and compare 24h P99 (owner: @sasha)
- carmen: roll back auto-rollback policy if experiment shows regression (owner: @carmen)

carmen: also add a short note to the runbook about temporary mitigation (headroom bump) and cost implications (extra reserved memory -> +3% unit cost).

liam: thanks. if perf-bot results look good we can land a kernel layout fix; otherwise we keep headroom + compaction tuning as a short-term mitigation. :thumbsup:

sasha: ack, I'll own the canary.

ajay: starting the trace run now, will paste raw nvprof snapshots when done.

perf-bot: exp/kal-2249991111 started at 2249991420 (ETA ~2h)
